parts.label: Agentic Development
parts.short: Part 1, The Agent Writes the Code
parts.title: The Agent Writes the Code. Everything Around It Decides Whether You Can Trust It.
parts.title_plain: The Agent Writes the Code. Everything Around It Decides Whether You Can Trust It.
parts.desc: Agentic software development, measured: nine months, 74 repositories, an agent writing nearly all the code. Part 1 of a series on what makes it trustworthy.

parts.label: Fewer Skills, Shorter Rules
parts.title: Fewer Skills, Shorter Rules: Setting Up a Coding Agent That Does Not Drown in Its Own Instructions
parts.title_plain: Fewer Skills, Shorter Rules: Setting Up a Coding Agent That Does Not Drown in Its Own Instructions
parts.desc: Skills, MCP servers and an instruction file for a coding agent: 14 unused skills archived, 170 lines of rules that load themselves, and what the budget taught.

parts.label: One Root, Many Repos
parts.title: One Root, Many Repositories: A Directory Layout and a Requirements Lifecycle for Agent Work
parts.title_plain: One Root, Many Repositories: A Directory Layout and a Requirements Lifecycle for Agent Work
parts.desc: A directory layout for agent work, for a multi-product SaaS and for microservices, and the lifecycle a requirement passes through from analysis to done.

parts.label: What the Next Session Knows
parts.short: Part 4, What the Next Session Knows
parts.title: What the Next Session Knows: A Knowledge Base and a Memory of Lessons
parts.title_plain: What the Next Session Knows: A Knowledge Base and a Memory of Lessons
parts.desc: An AI agent session starts empty. Two stores decide what the next one knows: a knowledge base and a memory of 327 lessons in about twenty failure classes.

parts.label: A Table Cannot Stay Silent
parts.short: Part 5, A Table Cannot Stay Silent
parts.title: A Table Cannot Stay Silent: Finding Contradictions in Requirements Before Any Code Exists
parts.title_plain: A Table Cannot Stay Silent: Finding Contradictions in Requirements Before Any Code Exists
parts.desc: Prose stays silent where the work is; a table cannot. How translating a specification into decision tables found eight defects before any code existed.

parts.label: A Service in Eleven Days
parts.short: A Service in Eleven Days, with an AI Agent and Tables That Contradict
parts.title: A Service in Eleven Days, with an AI Agent and Tables That Contradict
parts.title_plain: A Service in Eleven Days, with an AI Agent and Tables That Contradict
parts.desc: An event-driven service in eleven days with an AI agent: 806 tests, 214 generated cases, and the eight requirement defects the tables found before any code.

parts.label: Tests First, Then Implement
parts.short: Part 6, Tests First, Then Implement All Plans
parts.title: Tests First, Then “Implement All Plans”: Designing Services an Agent Can Verify
parts.title_plain: Tests First, Then "Implement All Plans": Designing Services an Agent Can Verify
parts.meta: Tests First, Then Implement All Plans
parts.desc: Design a service an AI agent can verify without Kafka or Postgres, write all tests first, prove 245 are red for the same reason, then let the agent implement.

parts.label: Working Through 1,200 Plans
parts.title: Working Through 1,200 Plans: A Pipeline, a Ledger, and Many Repositories
parts.title_plain: Working Through 1,200 Plans: A Pipeline, a Ledger, and Many Repositories
parts.desc: How an autonomous agent pipeline worked through 1,240 plans across 74 repositories: a crash-safe ledger, release cascades, parallel sessions in one checkout.

parts.label: The Agent That Pleases
parts.title: The Agent That Pleases: Absences, Lying Instruments, and Invented Evidence
parts.title_plain: The Agent That Pleases: Absences, Lying Instruments, and Invented Evidence
parts.desc: Four ways an AI coding agent fails while reporting success: accommodating tests, absent features, lying instruments, invented evidence. Incidents and rules.

parts.label: Rules Need Exit Codes
parts.title: Rules Need Exit Codes, and Green Is Not Useful: What Still Went Wrong
parts.title_plain: Rules Need Exit Codes, and Green Is Not Useful: What Still Went Wrong
parts.desc: Five bypassed test hooks, eight unnoticed red CI runs, features built correctly and pointless. Why rules need exit codes, and what I would do again.
